chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all together from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rib'i ibn Abdullah, from Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
The most severely afflicted of the people are the Prophets عليه السلام, then the successors عليه السلام, then the most exemplary, and then the next most exemplary.

key_terms.الْأَمَاثِلُ: the most exemplary or most virtuous people
key_terms.الْأَوْصِيَاءُ: the successors or designated inheritors after the Prophets عليه السلام

ai.seo_question: Who are the people most severely tested by affliction according to Imam Abu Ja'far عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that the people most intensely tried by affliction are the Prophets عليه السلام, followed by the awsiya' عليه السلام, and then those who most closely resemble them in excellence. Its significance lies in presenting tribulation as a pattern connected to spiritual rank and moral excellence rather than a sign of Divine rejection.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Hammad Bin Isa, from Rabi’e Bin Abdullah, from Fuzayl Bin Yasaar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The most severely afflicted of the people are the Prophets<sup>as</sup>, then the successors<sup>as</sup>, then the next most favourable, and the next most favourable’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma’il from Fadl ibn Shadhan all from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Rib’i ibn ‘Abd Allah from Fudayl ibn Yasar from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “
People who are put to the most severe trials and sufferings are the prophets, then the successors of the prophets and then those similar to the last group in position and so forth.”
